name: Hardcoded Alibaba/Tencent Cloud credentials or public OSS bucket ACL
attack_scenario: Attacker harvests the LTAI/AKID key from source or a bundle, calls the Aliyun/Tencent API to read OSS/COS buckets, spin up ECS instances, or pivot across the account; a PublicReadWrite bucket additionally lets anyone list, download, and overwrite (e.g. plant a webshell in) stored objects.
negative_test_hint: stage a file containing "LTAI5tGdstatic1234567890" and assert the secret-scanning gate blocks the commit because the key must come from the environment

exemplar.explanation: Alibaba Cloud AccessKey IDs (fixed LTAI prefix) and Tencent Cloud SecretIds (AKID plus 32 chars) are high-entropy credential signatures that scanners tuned only to AWS/Google formats miss; committed to source they are harvested to read OSS/COS buckets and pivot across the account, and a PublicReadWrite bucket ACL lets anyone list, download, and overwrite stored objects. Keys belong in environment variables or a secret manager, and buckets stay private.
